headline: GOLD RETREATS TO $4,365 AS PROFIT-TAKERS UNWIND CPI-FUELED RALLY — SILVER EASES TO $64; ANALYSTS SEE TREND INTACT
snippet: Physical gold fell $28 to $4,364.96 Friday as speculative money stepped aside following an inflation-fueled run to a two-month high. Silver slipped to $64.21/oz. Mixed signals drove the move: cooler July CPI trimmed rate-hike bets while firmer core PPI revived them. Reuters and USAGOLD frame the pullback as a lack of fresh catalysts, not a change in trend. Jackson Hole keynote on August 28 is the next major macro event.

headline: STEPPE GOLD (TSX: STGO) Q2 2026: REVENUE SURGES 91% TO $61.8M ON +73% GOLD PRODUCTION; ALL DEBT REPAID, GUIDANCE HELD
snippet: Mongolia-focused Steppe Gold posted Q2 revenue of $61.8 million vs. $32.3 million a year ago — a 91% jump driven by a 73% production increase to 22,465 oz and an average realized price of $4,493/oz. The company fully repaid all remaining debt, including its BORO bond and TDB Gold II loan, and maintained full-year production guidance of approximately 68,000 oz, a textbook example of operating leverage to higher gold prices.

headline: SLAM EXPLORATION (TSX-V: SXL) DRILLS 1.19% CuEq OVER 24.6m; NEW MASSIVE SULPHIDE DISCOVERY 2,000m NORTHWEST AT GOODWIN
snippet: SLAM Exploration drilled 1.19% copper equivalent over 24.6 metres in hole GW26-29 at the Goodwin Cu-Ni-Co project in British Columbia. A second hole, GW26-36, opened a new massive sulphide target 2,000 metres northwest of the Logan zone — a lateral extension that could materially expand the known mineralized footprint ahead of a resource estimate.

headline: COPPER SMASHES $14,455/TONNE ALL-TIME HIGH — AI DATA CENTRES AND POWER GRID BUILDOUT REPLACE EVs AS THE DEMAND ENGINE
snippet: Copper hit a new LME all-time high of $14,455/tonne in August 2026, driven by AI infrastructure construction and grid electrification investment rather than the EV narrative that dominated prior cycles. Codelco setbacks, DRC concentrate export restrictions, and Freeport-McMoRan smelter outages amplify the supply squeeze. Analysts project a structural deficit by 2035 that the current mine development pipeline cannot bridge.

headline: LITHIUM ARGENTINA (TSX: LAR) Q2 2026: CAUCHARI-OLAROZ DELIVERS US$141M FREE CASH FLOW — RUNNING AT 95% DESIGN CAPACITY
snippet: Lithium Argentina's Cauchari-Olaroz brine operation produced 9,280 tonnes of lithium carbonate at 95% of design capacity in Q2 2026, generating US$141 million in free cash flow from operations. The company swung to net income of $1.3M from a $4.1M loss a year prior and distributed $27M to shareholders post-quarter. A counterpoint to bearish lithium sentiment driven by Australian hard-rock mine restarts stoking 2027 supply fears.

headline: BARRICK + NEWMONT SEAL $1.95B NEVADA GOLD MINES DEAL — CREATES NEAR-100M-OZ COMPLEX AND CLEARS BARRICK NA IPO PATH
snippet: Barrick and Newmont resolved all outstanding Nevada Gold Mines JV disputes in a landmark deal announced August 10: Newmont pays Barrick $1.95 billion cash to fold Fourmile (Barrick) and Mike and Fiberline (Newmont) into the JV, creating a near-100-million-ounce gold complex in Nevada. Newmont also consented to Barrick's planned IPO of its North American gold assets, expected to close before year-end.

headline: CHINA'S H2 2026 RARE EARTH QUOTAS STILL UNPUBLISHED — THE SINGLE LARGEST OPEN CATALYST FOR THE SECTOR HEADING INTO SEPTEMBER
snippet: As of mid-August 2026, China has not published its second-half rare earth mining and smelting quotas — the number that historically sets the global supply ceiling for the entire sector. The absence of this data, combined with USA Rare Earth's Serra Verde shareholder vote on August 28, makes the next two weeks potentially pivotal for rare earth prices and North American producers.

headline: WEEKLY METALS RECAP AUG 14: GOLD AND SILVER HOLD KEY GAINS DESPITE FRIDAY PULLBACK; JACKSON HOLE IN FOCUS
snippet: The week ending August 14 saw gold hold near $4,400 and silver above $64 despite late profit-taking on mixed PPI data. Copper's record run continued. The week's key driver was the July CPI print on Wednesday, which briefly pushed silver to $67+ before the PPI trimmed those gains. All eyes shift to Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote on August 28 — the single most market-moving event for precious metals pricing in the near term.

headline: AFTER GOLD AND SILVER, IS COPPER SET FOR A BIG RUN? FOUR STOCKS ANALYSTS SAY ARE POSITIONED FOR THE NEXT MOVE
snippet: With gold at $4,400 and silver above $64, analyst attention is turning to copper: will speculative capital rotate into base metals as the rate picture clears? Four TSX and NYSE-listed names offering leveraged exposure to copper's record $14,000+ price are highlighted. The consensus view is that AI data centre and power grid infrastructure demand represents a multi-year tailwind still in its early innings.

headline: WHY IS SILVER GOING UP? MONEY METALS BREAKS DOWN THE SIX STRUCTURAL DRIVERS BEHIND SILVER'S RALLY TO $64+
snippet: Money Metals Exchange analysis examines the structural drivers behind silver's 2026 rally: six consecutive years of supply deficits, strong industrial demand, geopolitical pressures on mining supply chains, movement of physical silver between London and New York vaults, resilient Eastern investment demand, and the metal's historical role as a monetary hedge during periods of fiscal expansion and currency debasement.
